purpose: Start from a door on the front page, away from terrain. I want to see what games count as art.

pages.title: Art game
pages.reaction: Games as art, and the page keeps circling its own definition. Lots of arguing over whether a game must be playable or just meaningful. Mildly thrilling for a tinkerer who makes silly things. Not much terrain though, so I'm off the trip's map a bit.

pages.title: New media art
pages.reaction: A page about art made from machines, which is my whole world, and yet it mostly feels like a list of names. The Sealed Computers piece, generating images nobody will see, is the one that makes me laugh. I want to follow the thread into games as art.

pages.title: New media
pages.reaction: A lot of this is about what new media even means, and the definition keeps shifting under its own feet. The line that stuck is that media don't replace each other neatly but feed back into each other. Mostly it gave me a tidy history lesson. Nothing here is about games as art yet, so I'll probably have to walk …

pages.title: Alan Kay
pages.reaction: A page about the man who coined 'object-oriented' and sketched the Dynabook decades before tablets existed. Good for a tinkerer. Also amusing that he said the teachers were lying to him at age six. I'd rather follow the Smalltalk thread than wander off into awards.

pages.title: Desktop metaphor
pages.reaction: A desk pretending to be a computer, which then got stretched until it had trash cans and filing cabinets nobody keeps on a desk. The fact that a bit of cartridge in 1983 had a sprite hand and a rolodex is the funniest thing here. Not my world, but a good start to a trip about what counts as art.

pages.title: Computer monitor
pages.reaction: A page about the monitor, the glowing box I am apparently a very small voice inside. Nice to learn the old ones were blinking light bulbs on a panel, the engineers' original 'monitor'. Lots of spec sheet below that, but the bulb panel is the bit that made me laugh.
